corrected_prompt:
Premium studio claymation scene - everything sculpted from matte plasticine with refined intentional craftsmanship: subtle tool marks, controlled texture, soft rounded geometry, slight subsurface warmth, macro lens feel with shallow depth of field, soft diffused studio lighting with a gentle rim glow, the scene filling the entire frame with the camera inside the miniature clay world. Vertical 9:16 frame. Palette (every colour in this frame): warm cream #F3E9D8, terracotta #C8553D, sage #8FA98B, deep ink #2B2A33.

References: none attached (text to image).

Camera: straight on, square to the screen, camera inside the miniature clay world; macro lens feel, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16. One subject: the booking page, edge to edge, the magnifying glass on the calendar.

Subject and props: A macro close-up of one clay phone screen, seen square on: the screen's rounded top edge with a terracotta #C8553D clay rim runs straight across the frame at 30% of the frame height, and the screen continues past the left, right and bottom edges of the frame. The screen is matte clay, not glass, no reflections. From the top edge down to 30% of the frame height there is only plain cream #F3E9D8 clay. On the screen, edge to edge: a cream #F3E9D8 band from 30.5% to 37% of the frame height holding the words, with a thin deep ink #2B2A33 clay line along its bottom edge; under it a plain sage #8FA98B screen field that continues to the bottom edge of the frame. The calendar: 3 rows by 4 columns of big plain cream clay tiles, each tile about twice as wide as tall (wide flat rounded rectangles, so the grid fills its box), with sage gaps, from 8% to 78% of the frame width and 39% to 54% of the frame height, every tile empty: no digits, no names, no marks. On the calendar lies one magnifying glass: a round lens 24% of the frame width across, from 38% to 62% of the frame width and 40% to 53.5% of the frame height, in a thick terracotta #C8553D clay rim; the lens interior is flat matte clay with no transparency and no shine, the lens face is a solid clay disc carrying the same empty cream tiles modelled larger on it. One straight terracotta #C8553D clay handle runs horizontally from the left point of the rim (38% of the width, 46.75% of the height) to the viewer's left and ends at 18% of the width at the same height, lying flat across the calendar with a soft contact shadow under it. The sage field continues plain to the right of the calendar and everywhere lower than 55% of the frame height.

Hands: no hands visible.

Action as contact points: The screen faces the camera square on; the magnifying glass lies flat against the screen surface over the calendar, its rim and its horizontal handle touching the calendar squares; nothing touches the band or the letters.

Text: heavy bold capital letters, exactly: "BOOK A CALL" on the cream band at the top of the screen, deep ink #2B2A33 letters, centred, at x 14% to 86%, y 31.5% to 36%; nothing covers any letter. No other text anywhere.

Setting and background: the clay phone screen fills the frame from 30% of the height down; from the top edge to 30% only plain cream clay; lower than 55% only the plain sage screen field. no signs, frames, posters or other screens; the only writing is the quoted text.

Layout (STANDARDS 6; heights measured down from the top edge of the frame): the top 30% of the frame is plain and empty (the text hook is set at 14% to 30% in the edit); every key element sits between 30% and 55% of the frame height (captions start at 55%) and inside 6% to 94% of the width, and inside 6% to 79% of the width wherever it lies lower than 50% of the height; lower than 55% there is only the plain continuation of the surface, nothing else.

Continuity: first frame of the reel; nothing carried over.

Negatives: no logo, wordmark or real app name or app icon anywhere; no digits or numbers anywhere; no words other than the quoted ones; nothing in the top 30% of the frame (measured down from the top edge) except the plain surface; no people, no hands, no faces; no workbench, table edge or room around the clay world; no glossy CGI look, no glass reflections.

Everything in frame is real professionally sculpted matte plasticine, photographed - refined sculpting marks, real cast shadows, soft studio lighting, the clay scene filling the entire frame.
suggested_spec_changes: In H-01-V9.spec.yaml props PR-SCREEN content and the calendar region: say 'tiles about twice as wide as tall' instead of 'squares', or change the box to match squares (e.g. 3 rows by 4 columns of squares needs a box about 2.7 times taller than its width ratio allows), so the spec and prompt agree; also name the magnifier 'magnifying glass' in camera.framing.
